title: The classification is a decision record on the run branch
description:
Jev is asked ONCE per tick. The answer is written to the run branch as a decision record, like the review and closeout exchanges already are, so a restart re-reads it instead of re-asking a model it already paid.

This is axiom 1, not thrift, and the distinction decides the acceptance. Cold reconstruction from git must reach the SAME dispatch as the warm process. A recorded classification does. A re-ask only probably does - Jev is probabilistic, and two calls on the same tick may differ, which would make a cold re-derivation dispatch a different model than the run it is reconstructing. That is an axiom 1 violation wearing the costume of a cache miss.

Record the full distribution and the model identity, not just the chosen work type. The distribution is what the routing rule consumes, and recording only the argmax would mean a threshold change could not be re-evaluated against runs that already happened.

Follow whatever the review and closeout exchanges already do for record shape and location rather than inventing a third convention.
acceptance_criteria: A classification is written to the run branch once, later passes and a cold re-derivation from git read the record rather than calling the classifier, the recorded distribution is complete enough to re-evaluate a different threshold against it, and a re-derivation reaches the same dispatch as the warm process
